To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
global knowledge capitalism is a project of elite led, neoliberal policy makers and that it has resulted in a crisis of employability in South Korea.
the global economy is characterized by a new form of capitalism that is based on the creation of a global knowledge economy.
the neoliberal discourse of employability has become hegemonic in South Korea.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the state and the market in terms of education, the role of the state, and the role of the individual in a globalised world.

the way in which workers' employability is increasingly expected of them, and with the way in that the state is increasingly withdrawing from the provision of employment welfare in favour of individual self reliance and the development of self woven safety net.
the relationship between global knowledge capitalism and the crisis of employability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the global knowledge economy has resulted in a new form of capitalist coercion, which has resulted in the creation of a new form of worker subjectivity.

the neoliberal discourse surrounding employability has resulted in a form of global knowledge capitalism that has reduced workers to their ability to create self woven safety nets, and has thus resulted in a crisis of employability.
in the contemporary global economy, workers' employability is being increasingly defined as an individual's ability to create self woven safety nets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the context of the global knowledge economy, the state has become increasingly responsible for the provision of education and training to the individual, and the individual has become responsible for the provision and maintenance of employability.

in the global knowledge economy, workers have been expected to cultivate an increasingly diverse repertoire of skills in an immaterial work world in which they are to be self-reliant, self-entrepreneurial and self-organising.

the neoliberal discourse of employability has become a hegemonic force in South Korea and that it is the result of the elite class in South Korea, the Korean government, and international institutions, such as the OECD, the World Bank, and the IMF.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the neoliberal discourse surrounding employability is not simply about individual workers, but is also about the creation of a new subjectivity of workers as self responsible and self reliant individuals, which is a form of social control in the post industrial era.
the global economy is a place of opportunity for the privileged few and the rest of the population is expected to be self reliant and to be able to create their own opportunities.
the global economy has become a site of knowledge capitalism and that the new form of coercion is the creation of self woven social safety nets.
